title: Single Letter Sounds
keyIdea: Each letter has a name and a sound. The name of m is em, but the sound it makes in a word is mmm. When you read, you use the sound. Say sounds short and pure, mmm not muh. The five vowels a, e, i, o and u have a short sound, like a in cat, and they can also say their name, like o in go.

kid: Every letter has a name. This is m. Its name is em. But in a word, m says mmm. Hum it: mmm, like moon.
To read, we use the sound, not the name. c is called see. But in cat it says k. So cat is k, a, t.
Keep each sound short. Say mmm, not muh. Say sss, not suh. Then the sounds join up to make a word.
a, e, i, o and u are vowels. They have short sounds: a like apple, e like egg, i like insect, o like octopus, u like umbrella. A vowel can also say its name. In go, o says oh.
adult: This is grapheme-phoneme correspondence, the first step of systematic synthetic phonics. A grapheme is a written letter or group of letters; a phoneme is a single speech sound. Single letter sounds match one letter to its most common phoneme. The EYFS early learning goal asks children to say a sound for each letter of the alphabet, CCSS RF.K.3a asks for the primary sound of each consonant, and RF.K.3b asks for the short and long sounds of the five major vowels. In England, Year 1 children should respond speedily with the correct sound to each grapheme.

Key words: letter name, letter sound (phoneme), grapheme, consonant, vowel, short vowel, long vowel, initial sound, medial sound and CVC word (consonant, vowel, consonant, like cat or bed). A long vowel says its letter name: o in go, e in me, i in hi.

Common mistakes: giving the letter name instead of the sound (see for c), adding an uh to sounds (muh, suh, tuh), which makes blending hard because m-a-t becomes muh-a-tuh; mixing up b and d, which face different ways; and mixing up short e and short i, which sound close in bed and bid. Be careful to stretch continuous sounds (mmm, sss, fff) and keep bouncy ones (b, d, t) short and crisp.

In the lab your child flips letter tiles to see each sound and a picture, drags pictures to the letter that makes their first sound, fills in the missing middle vowel of a CVC word, sorts words by whether the vowel is short or says its name, and plays a quick-sounds round. Every drag has a big button twin.

familyTip: Play I spy with sounds, not names: 'I spy something that starts with mmm.' Keep the sound pure. When your child guesses, say the word slowly together, mmm-oo-n, and check the first sound.

visual.caption: Which sound does it start with? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: flip letter tiles, match pictures to first sounds, fill the middle vowel and sort short and long vowels.

practice.prompt: Single letter sounds: the letter s is called ess. What sound does it make at the start of sun?
practice.hint: Say sun slowly. Listen to the very first sound. Keep it pure, with no uh.
practice.explain: s says sss, like a snake. Ess is its name, and suh adds an extra uh sound.

practice.prompt: The word cat has 3 letters, and each letter makes one sound. How many sounds are in {n} words like cat?
practice.hint: Each word like cat has 3 sounds: k, a, t. Count 3 for each word.
practice.explain: {n} words with 3 sounds each make {=3*n} sounds. In cat, c says k, a says a, t says t.

practice.prompt: Which picture word starts with the sound b?
practice.hint: Say each word. Which one starts with a short b sound? Watch out: d faces the other way.
practice.explain: Bus starts with b. Dog starts with d, and pig starts with p, which is a puff of air.

practice.prompt: You know {n} letter sounds. Today you learn 2 more. How many letter sounds do you know now?
practice.hint: Start at {n} and count on 2 more.
practice.explain: {n} and 2 more make {=n+2} letter sounds. A few new sounds each week adds up.

pool.prompt: The letter c is called see. What sound does c make at the start of cat?
pool.hint: Say cat slowly. Is the first sound like see, or like k?
pool.explain: In cat, c says k. See is the name of the letter, not its sound.

pool.prompt: Which is the best way to say the sound of m?
pool.hint: Keep the sound pure. Hum it with your lips shut.
pool.explain: m says mmm. Muh adds an extra sound, and em is the letter's name.

pool.prompt: Which word has a short a sound, like apple?
pool.hint: Say each word slowly and listen to the middle sound.
pool.explain: Cat has a in the middle, like apple. Cot has o, and cut has u.

pool.prompt: In bed, what is the middle sound?
pool.hint: Say b-e-d slowly. e and i sound close, so listen carefully.
pool.explain: Bed has a short e in the middle, like egg. With i it would be bid.

pool.prompt: In the word go, what does the o say?
pool.hint: Say go. Does the o sound like octopus, or like the letter's own name?
pool.explain: In go, the o says its name, oh. That is a long vowel. In dog, the o is short.

pool.prompt: Which letter makes the first sound in dog?
pool.hint: Say dog slowly. b and d look alike, so check which way the letter faces.
pool.explain: Dog starts with d. b faces the other way and says b, like bus. g is at the end of dog.

pool.prompt: You flip {n} letter tiles, and each tile shows one sound. How many sounds do you see?
pool.hint: One tile shows one sound. Count the tiles.
pool.explain: Each single letter tile shows one sound, so {n} tiles show {n} sounds.

pool.prompt: Which word starts with the same sound as fish?
pool.hint: Fish starts with fff. Say each word and listen to its first sound.
pool.explain: Fan starts with fff, like fish. Van starts with vvv, which is close but buzzes, and pan starts with p.

pool.prompt: Sam knows {n} letter sounds. This week he learns the sounds for s, a, t and p. How many letter sounds does Sam know now?
pool.hint: Count the new letters: s, a, t, p. Then start at {n} and count on that many.
pool.explain: s, a, t and p are 4 new sounds. {n} and 4 more make {=n+4} letter sounds.
